workUnit: SmartAIHub R5 SPEC-304 trusted local ingress to persisted SPEC-269 Project memory

acceptance.positive: A locally HMAC-signed, short-lived assertion from the test-only ingress producer was consumed through HTTP by createContextWithTrustedAppIngress; the active DB custom-domain alias resolved to the canonical App and buildChatContext read that App-bound Project memory from PostgreSQL.
negativeCases: Host and X-Forwarded-Host alone yielded trustedAppContext=null; Global memory remained available and Project memory was absent.
A replayed assertion was rejected and Project memory was absent.
A validly signed same-tenant assertion binding another App to this App's alias was rejected.
A validly signed cross-tenant identity was rejected against the authenticated tenant.

database.name: miniapp_r5_test
database.schema: Curated R5 current-schema test projection plus existing additive SPEC-304 migration 0392; no historical migration chain
database.migrationScope: 0392 was applied only to the authorized disposable miniapp_r5_test database.

reviewedSecurityLenses: Assertion HMAC uses 32 random bytes per test; no production or repository secret is read.
Signature comparison is constant-time after length validation; malformed encodings fail closed.
Assertion IDs are consumed once; replay cannot regain App context.
Issuer and audience are exact server-owned expectations and timestamps are validated by the canonical assertion consumer.
Authenticated user and tenant come from the server-side SDK test binding; request Host and X-Forwarded-Host do not select tenant or App.
Custom-domain resolution uses the canonical database alias repository, current tenant, alias status, and App lifecycle.
A signed App identity that conflicts with the currently resolved alias is rejected even within the same tenant.
Cross-tenant assertion claims are rejected against the authenticated tenant before memory access.
Fresh Project membership and App-Project binding checks remain in the persisted runtime path; existing revocation cases still pass.
Untrusted contexts retain permitted Global memory while Project-scoped memory stays out of the prompt.
The context permission ceiling keeps durable Project-shared writes disabled; this test performs reads only.
The runner requires the exact loopback database and explicit disposable confirmation, uses only synthetic fixtures, and applies only the existing additive 0392 schema there.
limitations: The signing producer is a test-only local boundary; this is not evidence of a production Cloudflare or external-edge assertion producer.
The SDK authentication result is bound to a synthetic account fixture; no production authentication or public ingress was exercised.
No worker-crossing App context was tested.
App-private memory isolation remains unavailable in the current persistence model.
SPEC-269 T-01 through T-23 remain partial; this evidence does not close any full Spec.
